This announcement will be used to fill the current Regional Wildlife Manager vacancies in Coeur d’Alene and Pocatello only. To be considered for either current vacancy for Regional Wildlife Manager, you must apply through this announcement. 

Responsibilities: 

As a regional wildlife manager, you will oversee a dedicated wildlife team charged with implementation of regional and statewide management priorities for a variety of wildlife species and their habitats, including big game, upland game, migratory birds, waterfowl, forest carnivores, species of greatest conservation need, and furbearers, as well as implementation of the State Wildlife Action Plan.

Develops and monitors program budget.

The Wood Lab of Ecology and Ecosystems Studies at Tennessee Tech. University is looking for a Master of Science student to work on an environmental microbiology project, focusing on antibiotic-resistant genes in urban streams in the Cookeville, TN area.

Project Overview: A M.S. graduate assistantship is available to study antibiotic-resistant genes (ARGs) in streams in the Appalachian Plateau and Cookeville, TN area. Working in streams in both urban and rural landscapes, the position will quantify seasonal changes in ARGs in streams in the Cookeville, TN area as the streams move through the city limits of Cookeville, into a predominantly rural landscape, and into a large reservoir. Description
*Applications are reviewed on a rolling-basis and applications may close before the deadline.

APHIS Office/Lab and Location: Three research opportunities are currently available with the U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA), Animal Plant Health Inspection Service (APHIS), located in Fort Collins, Colorado.

The Animal and Plant Health Inspection Service (APHIS) is a multi-faceted Agency with a broad mission area that includes protecting and promoting U.S. agricultural health, regulating genetically engineered organisms, administering the Animal Welfare Act and carrying out wildlife damage management activities. These efforts support the overall mission of USDA, which is to protect and promote food, agriculture, natural resources and related issues. APHIS' mission also includes addressing issues such as wildlife damage and disease management; regulation of genetically engineered crops and animal welfare; and protection of public health and safety as well as natural resources that are vulnerable to invasive pests and pathogens.

Research Project: You will learn through collaboration with veterinary medical officers, statisticians, economists, entomologists, and ecologists who specialize in epidemiology, risk analysis, disease modeling, economic evaluation, and surveillance. You will gain experience contributing to the development and operationalization of analytical tools and understanding how they support national and regional risk assessments, emergency preparedness, response, and surveillance planning for New World Screwworm (NWS) in wildlife and domestic livestock populations.

Learning Objectives: This fellowship will provide opportunities for you to learn about and aid in the development and operationalizing analytical tools that support national scale programmatic decisions and policy. Under the guidance of a mentor, you will:

Expand experience analyzing domestic livestock, wildlife, and New World Screwworm (NWS) fly surveillance data while accounting for environmental and biological factors that influence NWS occurrence. 
Cultivate analytical skills in developing methods to evaluate surveillance sensitivity and detection probability, determine optimal spatial and temporal surveillance strategies, and forecast surveillance priorities in wildlife and domestic livestock populations under future environmental conditions. 
Build experience in developing and applying statistical and mathematical models of New World Screwworm (NWS) population dynamics, including reproduction, survival, movement, and spread, while learning to incorporate environmental and weather factors into modeling.
Gain experience using both recent and historical data to evaluate surveillance, mitigation, and prevention strategies. 
Strengthen skills in integrating diverse qualitative and quantitative information, documenting methods and assumptions, communicating findings to varied audiences, and collaborating with SMEs and policymakers.
Develop practical knowledge of disease risk modeling and learn to translate analytical results into tools that address program needs. 
Mentor: The mentor for this opportunity is Katie Portacci ([email removed]). If you have questions about the nature of the research, please contact the mentor.

Anticipated Appointment Start Date: January 2027.  Start date is flexible and will depend on a variety of factors.

Appointment Length: The appointment will initially be for two years but may be extended upon recommendation of USDA APHIS and is contingent on the availability of funds.

Level of Participation: The appointment is full time.

Citizenship Requirements: This opportunity is available to U.S. citizens.

ORISE Information: This program, administered by ORAU through its contract with the U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) to manage the Oak Ridge Institute for Science and Education (ORISE), was established through an interagency agreement between DOE and APHIS. Participants do not become employees of USDA, APHIS, DOE or the program administrator, and there are no employment-related benefits. Proof of health insurance is required for participation in this program. Health insurance can be obtained through ORISE.

Questions: Please visit our Program Website. After reading, if you have additional questions about the application process, please email [email removed] and include the reference code for this opportunity.

Qualifications
The qualified candidate should have received or be currently pursuing a master's or doctoral degree in one of the relevant fields.

Preferred skills:

Experience in biological, population, or epidemiological modeling and spatial analysis, including population dynamics, infectious disease and ecological processes.   
Strong quantitative skills in Bayesian statistics, machine learning, advanced statistical approaches, geospatial and mathematical modeling in an applied setting.  
Experience with integrated population models or knowledge of their development and application. 
Experience with study design and integrating observational field and experimental data into modeling frameworks.  
Proficiency in R, python, C++, GitHub, ESRI, Bayesian computational methods using MCMC frameworks (e.g., JAGS, STAN, NIMBLE) and mathematical approaches (e.g. ordinary differential equations). 
Strong communication skills, including the ability to communicate complex modeling results.

Description
Job Title: Forest Manager

Location: Hawai‘i Island

About Forest Solutions:

Forest Solutions Inc. (FSI) has been Hawaiʻi’s leading forestry and land management company for over 30 years, specializing in large-scale tree planting, invasive species control, wildfire prevention, native forest restoration, timber plantation management, forest inventory, agroforestry, permitting, and community engagement. We help Hawaiʻi Grow! 

As a team-oriented small business, FSI brings together project managers, foresters, natural resource specialists, technicians, and field crews to address Hawaiʻi’s unique land management challenges. Our work is rooted in scientific best practices, field expertise, and a deep connection to Hawaiʻi’s biocultural heritage. FSI has played a key role in shaping large-scale forest management, including supporting active management of over 500,000 acres per year and planting over 1,000,000 native plants across more than 5,000 acres, including the largest native forest restoration project in the state.

This is an opportunity to be part of a diverse and impactful team working on meaningful conservation efforts in Hawaiʻi’s stunning and rugged landscapes.

About the Job:

We are seeking a versatile Forest Manager to oversee end-to-end operations across our forestry, wildfire mitigation and fuel reduction, vegetation management, ecological restoration, and natural resource projects across Hawaiʻi. This is a full-time, year-round position with supervisory responsibilities. Reporting to a Senior Forester, this position bridges technical project administration and hands-on operational side of natural resource management. The candidate will be expected to take projects from initial planning and proposal development through budgeting, scheduling, field implementation, monitoring, reporting, and client communication. The position requires someone who can independently manage multiple projects at once while coordinating field crews, subcontractors, landowners, agencies, and other project partners.

This position requires someone who thrives in a highly variable environment, with roughly 60% of your time spent outdoors in variable weather and 40% in the office. Field conditions often involve remote off-road driving, cross-country hiking sometimes 10+ miles off trail, navigating thick rain forests as well as dry, hot environments, and conducting quality control checks across projects ranging from small parcels to landscape-scale efforts spanning tens of thousands of acres. Office time is reserved for GIS/drone data processing, supply procurement, maintenance logging, taking client & internal meetings, budgeting, proposal creation, and project planning and reporting. Work is project-based and highly responsive to client needs and timelines. Schedule flexibility, a sense of purpose, and self-motivation are essential, in addition to technical skills. 

The work location is variable on Hawaiʻi Island. Due to emergency response needs, the candidate must reside on or relocate to Hawaiʻi Island. The day-to-day locations can change as our client mix and project priorities change. We have projects throughout Hawaiʻi Island, and a few on the other Hawaiian Islands, and help each other out when needed. Occasional travel should be expected.


Candidate Selection Criteria:

Candidates will be evaluated for Entry, Mid, or Senior placement based on their background and professional experience in forestry, natural resource management, environmental science, conservation biology, ecology, wildlife management, or a related field.

For Entry-Level Placement, candidates must possess a relevant Bachelor’s degree along with a minimum of 2-3 years of relevant field experience. 
For Mid-Level Placement, candidates must possess both a relevant Bachelor’s and Master’s degree combined with 5-8 years of progressive field experience.
For Senior-Level Placement, candidates must possess at least a relevant Master’s degree alongside 10 or more years of extensive industry experience.

An equivalent combination of relevant field experience, specialized training, and education will be considered in lieu of the formal degree requirements for each level. 

Principal Responsibilities:

Manage multiple forestry, wildfire mitigation, vegetation management, restoration, and natural resource projects simultaneously.
Develop project scopes, budgets, cost estimates, schedules, work plans, proposals, and technical reports.
Coordinate field crews, subcontractors, equipment, materials, and project logistics.
Provide direct supervision, mentoring, and administrative oversight for assigned Forestry Technicians, as well as operational supervision of field crews and personnel at active project sites. 
Serve as a primary point of contact for clients, landowners, agencies, contractors, and project partners.
Conduct field assessments and translate field conditions into practical management recommendations.
Develop and implement wildfire mitigation and fuels-management projects, including fuel reduction, access improvements, vegetation management, and long-term maintenance strategies.
Support native forest restoration and reforestation projects, including site preparation, species selection, planting layouts, irrigation/water systems, invasive species management, maintenance, and monitoring.
Plan and oversee invasive plant and vegetation-management programs, including large landscape-scale treatment programs.
Use ArcGIS Pro, GPS/remote sensing, aerial imagery, and other geospatial information to develop project maps, treatment units, monitoring information, acreage calculations, and management recommendations.
Track project budgets, production, labor, materials, subcontractor costs, and overall project progress.
Prepare client reports, grant deliverables, maps, presentations, management plans, and other technical documents.
Assist with grant proposals, RFP responses, contract development, and new project/business-development opportunities.
Conduct field inspections and quality-control checks to ensure work meets project specifications and client expectations.
Help identify more efficient ways to complete field work and scale operations while maintaining quality and safety.
Be willing to spend time in the field when necessary rather than managing projects exclusively from an office.
Other duties as assigned.


Essential Qualifications:

Willingness and ability to work alone or in small teams in remote locations, with little or no mobile phone coverage
Able to confidently work with community groups and people with diverse backgrounds & occupations in a respectful manner
Physically able to walk long distances in rugged terrain, over sharp lava fields or in thick forests for a full workday collecting field data in all weather.  Ability to lift 75 lbs.
Experience operating small gas-powered tools safely such as weed eaters, chainsaw
Experience in the use of a computer and Google suite & Microsoft Office suite, knowledge of ESRI ArcGIS software, able to upload/download GPS data
Willing to mix and apply pesticides and chemical fertilizers in strict accordance with label requirements; certified applicator a plus
Strong written communication skills, particularly technical reports, management plans, proposals, scopes of work, and client correspondence.
Experience developing budgets, estimates, schedules, and scopes of work.
Able to drive and tow trailers with 4WD, manual transmission vehicles on rough roads; valid US driver’s license at the time of hire
Able to legally work in the United States at the time of hire


Desirable Qualifications:

Ability to speak or understand languages other than English; primarily Spanish and ʻŌlelo Hawaiʻi
Demonstrated project-management experience or evidence of being able to independently manage complex projects. 
Demonstrated ability to supervise or coordinate field crews and contractors.
Comfortable communicating directly with clients, landowners, government agencies, and project partners.
Wildfire mitigation/fuels experience; certifications a plus
Grant-funded project management
Experience working with heavy-equipment operators and contractors


Compensation & Benefits:

Competitive compensation starts at $60,000 - $80,000+ per year, commensurate with experience; optional vehicle stipend provided for use of personal truck for work & off-road driving, or use of company vehicles; 401K retirement plan; comprehensive healthcare (medical, dental, vision) with 100% employer-paid premiums for the employee; and PTO & sick leave policy plus holiday pay.

How to Apply:

If interested, please submit:
Cover letter highlighting abilities relevant to this position
Résumé or CV
List of at least 3 references we can contact

Electronically to: [email removed]

Equal Opportunity & Accessibility Statement:

Forest Solutions Inc. is an equal opportunity employer. We do not discriminate on the basis of disability, race, gender, religion, or any other protected status. We are committed to providing reasonable accommodations to qualified individuals with disabilities. If you require accommodations during the application process or in performing this role, please contact us to discuss your needs.

Forest Solutions Recruiting Team
8087769900

Description
Job Title: Operations Forester

Location: Hawai‘i Island

About Forest Solutions:

Forest Solutions Inc. (FSI) has been Hawaiʻi’s leading forestry and land management company for over 30 years, specializing in large-scale tree planting, invasive species control, wildfire prevention, native forest restoration, timber plantation management, forest inventory, agroforestry, permitting, and community engagement. We help Hawaii Grow! 

As a team-oriented small business, FSI brings together project managers, foresters, natural resource specialists, technicians, and field crews to address Hawaiʻi’s unique land management challenges. Our work is rooted in scientific best practices, field expertise, and a deep connection to Hawai‘i’s biocultural heritage. FSI has played a key role in shaping large-scale forest management, including supporting active management of over 500,000 acres per year and planting over 1,000,000 native plants across more than 5,000 acres, including the largest native forest restoration project in the state.

This is an opportunity to be part of a diverse and impactful team working on meaningful conservation efforts in Hawaiʻi’s stunning and rugged landscapes.


About the Job:

We are seeking a motivated and detail-oriented Operations Forester to support and lead field-based forest management projects across Hawai‘i Island. This position may be filled at a mid- to senior-level Operations Forester capacity, depending on candidate experience. This position, reporting to our Senior Forester, blends ecological knowledge with hands-on operational leadership and construction oversight in remote and challenging environments. Hawaiʻi’s native forests are among the most ecologically vibrant (and threatened) in the world. If you are driven by the challenge of removing invasive competitors to give native ecosystems room to breathe and thrive, this role offers you the platform, equipment, and scale to make a permanent, positive mark on Hawaiʻi Island’s landscapes.

This position requires someone who thrives in a highly variable environment, with roughly 60% of your time spent outdoors in variable weather and 40% in the office. Field conditions often involve remote off-road driving, cross-country hiking sometimes 10+ miles off trail, navigating thick rain forests as well as dry, hot environments, and conducting quality control checks across projects ranging from small parcels to landscape-scale efforts spanning tens of thousands of acres, with an expectation of 2–3 helicopter flights per year for remote field operations. Office time is reserved for GIS/drone data processing, supply procurement, maintenance logging, taking client & internal meetings, budgeting, proposal creation, and project planning and reporting. Work is project-based and highly responsive to client needs and timelines. Schedule flexibility, a sense of purpose, and self-motivation are essential, in addition to technical skills. 
This role is focused on implementing and managing projects such as wildfire mitigation and fuel reduction, landscape-scale invasive species management, erosion control, large-scale planting operations, access development, and forestry operations. The Operations Forester works closely with the Senior Forester to plan and execute projects, supervise field crews and subcontractors, oversee heavy equipment operations, and ensure work is completed safely, efficiently, and in alignment with ecological objectives.

The ideal candidate is comfortable operating at the intersection of science and agricultural/forestry field operations and able to interpret ecological goals and translate them into practical, on-the-ground implementation strategies. This is an opportunity to work on the frontlines protecting Hawai‘i’s unique biodiversity & ecosystems from aggressive invasive species. This isn't just vegetation management—it's active ecological recovery. You will see the direct results of your labor as treated units transform back into thriving, self-sustaining native Hawaiian habitats. A strong background in ecology, forestry, environmental impacts, or natural resource management, along with excellent organizational and leadership skills, is desirable. 

Flexibility, a sense of purpose, and self-motivation are essential, in addition to technical skills. This is a full-time, year-round position with supervisory responsibilities. Depending on experience, this role may involve supporting project leads or independently managing projects from planning through completion. 

Work locations vary widely and often involve off-road travel throughout Hawaiʻi Island with occasional off-island assignments. This role requires adaptability, strong leadership, sound judgment in remote settings, and the ability to manage evolving project priorities in response to client needs and environmental conditions.

Candidate Selection Criteria:
Candidates will be evaluated for Entry, Mid, or Senior placement based on their background and professional experience in forestry, botany, natural resource management, agriculture, environmental science, conservation biology, ecology, wildlife management, or a related field.

For Entry-Level Placement, candidates must possess a relevant Bachelor’s degree along with a minimum of 2-3 years of relevant field experience. 
For Mid-Level Placement, candidates must possess both a relevant Bachelor’s and Master’s degree combined with 5-8 years of progressive field experience.
For Senior-Level Placement, candidates must possess at least a relevant Master’s degree alongside 10 or more years of extensive industry experience.

An equivalent combination of relevant field experience, specialized training, and education will be considered in lieu of the formal degree requirements for each level. 


Principal Responsibilities:
Assist Senior Operations Forester with project organization, planning, managing field crews & subcontractors, tracking work progress, and inspecting the quality of fieldwork.
Oversee operational safety protocols and OSHA compliance across active field sites, conducting regular hazard assessments, holding safety briefings, and implementing continuous safety improvements.
Collect, process and analyze GPS and GIS data for mapping, reporting, and operational planning.
Supervise heavy equipment operations – site preparation, road maintenance, maintaining equipment maintenance logs.
Ensure the correct use and maintenance of field equipment, tractors, skidder, excavator, crawler tractors, review equipment use logs.
Apply and supervise the application of pesticides in accordance with the label and legal requirements, including personal protective equipment (PPE), verifying correct application methods and safety standards by field crews.
Represent company or clients at public and private meetings in a professional manner.
Assist in preparing annual work budgets, project proposals, and estimating the cost of completing projects.
Plan and track large-scale vegetation management operations using GIS/GPS data, including treatment boundaries, completed acreage, production rates, and field accomplishments for client reporting.
Prepare clear operational reports documenting completed work, acreage, crew and equipment production, field conditions, and project progress.
Help manage large-scale biomass processing and chipping operations, coordinating material handling, equipment, crews, production, and site logistics.
Coordinate preventative maintenance, routine inspections, troubleshooting, and repair scheduling for forestry and biomass-processing equipment, including large chippers (over 18in).
Track equipment productivity, downtime, maintenance needs, and operating costs to help improve project efficiency and future estimating.
Other duties as assigned.


Essential Qualifications:
Willingness and ability to work alone or in small teams in remote locations, with little or no mobile phone coverage.
Working knowledge of field safety practices, hazard recognition, and standard OSHA safety compliance guidelines.
Physically able to walk long distances in rugged terrain, over sharp lava fields or in thick forests for a full workday collecting field data in all weather. Ability to lift 75 lbs.
Experience operating small powered tools safely such as weed eaters, chainsaw, pruners, etc.
Experience in the use of a computer and Microsoft Office suite, basic knowledge of ESRI ArcGIS software, able to upload/download GPS data.
Willing to mix and apply pesticides and chemical fertilizers in strict accordance with label requirements; certified applicator a plus.
Able to drive and tow trailers with 4WD, manual transmission vehicles on rough roads; valid US driver’s license at the time of hire.
Able to legally work in the United States at the time of hire.
Working knowledge of preventative maintenance and basic mechanical troubleshooting for forestry and heavy equipment, including the ability to identify mechanical issues before they result in major equipment failure.
Ability to safely plan and coordinate work around large forestry equipment, including chippers, excavators, dozers, tractors, and material-handling equipment.

Desirable Qualifications:
Knowledge of the ecology of native Hawaiian flora and fauna.
Formal safety certifications a plus (e.g., OSHA 10/30-Hour General Industry/Construction, First Aid/CPR/Wilderness First Responder).
Experience planning or supervising large-scale vegetation management operations, including tracking acres treated, production rates, crew performance, and project costs.
Experience operating, maintaining, or managing industrial forestry or biomass-processing equipment, particularly large whole-tree chippers/grinders.
Strong working knowledge of ArcGIS Pro for operational mapping, treatment tracking, acreage calculations, and preparation of client-ready maps and reports.
Supervisory experience, including as a team leader.
Speak or understand languages other than English; primarily Spanish and ʻŌlelo Hawaiʻi.


Compensation & Benefits:
Competitive compensation starts at $60,000 - $80,000+ per year, commensurate with experience; optional vehicle stipend provided for use of personal truck for work & off-road driving, or use of company vehicles; 401K retirement plan; comprehensive healthcare (medical, dental, vision) with 100% employer-paid premiums for the employee; and PTO & sick leave policy plus holiday pay.


How to Apply:
If interested, please submit:
Cover letter highlighting abilities relevant to this position
Résumé or CV
List of at least 3 references we can contact

Electronically to: [email removed]

We are committed to providing reasonable accommodations to qualified individuals with disabilities. If you require accommodations during the application process or in performing this role, please contact us to discuss your needs.

Description
The Department of Environment and Society (ENVS) in the S.J. and Jessie E. Quinney College of Agriculture and Natural Resources (QANR) at Utah State University (USU) invites applications for a tenure-track position of Assistant Professor with expertise in the geography and human dimensions of environmental hazards and disaster risk. We seek a faculty member whose teaching and research will strengthen Utah’s ability to reduce hazard risks, protect people and infrastructure, and prepare for, respond to, and recover from disasters. The successful candidate will apply social and/or behavioral sciences to advance understanding and mitigation of risks from environmental hazards such as air pollution, droughts, earthquakes, extreme heat, flooding, and/or wildfire, including in the context of a changing climate and with relevance to the state of Utah. 
 This is a teaching excellence position, with an emphasis distribution of 60% teaching/advising, 30% research, and 10% service. This tenure-track, full-time academic year (nine-month) position is based at the USU main campus in Logan. The position will start August 2027. Background information is available on the webpages for the Department of Environment and Society and its home, the S.J. and Jessie E. Quinney College of Agriculture and Natural Resources.
 Application review begins December 10, 2026. The position will remain open until filled, but application by the date above is encouraged for full consideration. Candidates from all backgrounds and populations are encouraged to apply. For further information contact the search committee chair, Dr. Courtney Flint ([email removed]).
 Responsibilities:
The successful candidate will develop an outstanding teaching and mentoring program to support student success in both the Department’s academic programs and the University’s Center for Civic Excellence. The teaching role will include preparing students to understand environmental hazard risks, communicate about risks, evaluate risk-reduction strategies, and support mitigation and preparedness activities.
Teaching includes courses that contribute to the University’s General Education program and to the Department’s majors in environmental studies, environmental science and sustainability, geography, and recreation resource management. The successful candidate could expect to teach courses in hazards and society and to contribute to other departmental and Center for Civic Excellence curricular areas depending on specific expertise. 
The successful candidate will also provide leadership for a shared departmental commitment to community-engaged, experiential education for our undergraduate students, including, for example, leading projects with Utah communities and public agencies that develop skills relevant to environmental hazard mitigation, public safety, and emergency management.
The successful candidate will lead a research program investigating individual or community decision-making in the context of environmental hazards and disaster risk reduction.  
Student advising includes mentoring undergraduate researchers and advising graduate students in a supportive learning environment that promotes the success of all students.
Courses may be taught at both undergraduate and graduate levels and may be delivered in person, via virtual or online learning, or in a blended format. 
Service includes participation in university faculty duties and wider professional involvement.
 Minimum Qualifications:
An earned PhD at date-of-hire in geography or a related field, with background in environmental hazards and society.
 Preferred Qualifications:
A prior teaching and mentoring record that demonstrates potential for teaching excellence.
Demonstrated interest in community-engaged and experiential learning that complements USU’s Land Grant mission. 
Demonstrated application of research to understanding and mitigating the impacts of hazards through social and behavioral science perspectives.
A publication record consistent with career stage.
Demonstrated potential to build and maintain an effective research program, including the ability to secure funding.
Evidence of successful collaboration with natural and social scientists as well as practitioners across disciplines.
Experience with or the desire to learn about virtual and online course delivery. 
Demonstrated ability to contribute to a learning community of members from a range of backgrounds and experiences and to foster a sense of belonging for all students.
 To Apply: Applicants must submit all application materials electronically via the Utah State University Human Resources website: https://careers-usu.icims.com/jobs/10901/assistant-professor---environmental-risk-and-society/job.  Along with completing the online application, applicants will upload or insert the following:
Cover letter (2-page maximum)
CV
Research statement that covers research experience and interests (2-page maximum)
Teaching statement that covers teaching experience and philosophy, including in fostering the success of students from all backgrounds (2-page maximum)
Contact information for three references
 College/Department Highlights
The Department of Environment and Society applies social, environmental, and interdisciplinary sciences to understand human-environment interactions at a range of scales. Our faculty address complex environmental and societal challenges through innovative research and extension, generating practical insights for managers, policymakers, and practitioners. We provide graduate and undergraduate education in environmental, social and interdisciplinary sciences, recreation resource management, and geography. Together, we value holistic practices and community engagement for a more sustainable tomorrow.
 The S.J. & Jessie E. Quinney College of Agriculture & Natural Resources (QANR) at USU is known for its research, traditions, and community engagement, with recent highlights including new leadership, special events, and innovative projects. QANR offers 12 departments covering agriculture, food, environment, technology, design, and more, plus associate degrees and technical certificates at statewide campuses.
 University Highlights
As Utah’s student-centered, land-grant research university, Utah State University expands opportunity and strengthens communities across the state through learning, discovery, extension, and engagement. Founded in 1888, USU now holds two Carnegie distinctions: R1 status for very high research activity and the Carnegie Community Engagement Classification. Its innovative research and scholarship is grounded in reciprocal partnerships with local, regional, and global communities, advancing knowledge and serving the public good across Utah, the nation, and the world. With over 50 world-class research facilities and the nation’s second-oldest undergraduate research program, USU prepares students to become active, civically engaged leaders who can address critical societal challenges.
 USU enrolls over 29,800 students, both online and in person at locations throughout the state. Utah State’s 30 locations include a main campus in Logan, Utah, residential campuses in Price and Blanding, and six additional statewide campuses, along with education centers serving every county. USU educates students from all 50 states and more than 80 countries. For over 100 years, USU Extension has served and engaged Utahns, serving every county in the state.
 Competing at the NCAA Division I level in 16 sports, USU is a proud member of the Pac-12 Conference, which it joined July 1, 2026. The Aggies capped a historic final season in the Mountain West by capturing nine combined regular-season and tournament titles in 2025-26, with five teams advancing to postseason play. This tradition of excellence extends to the classroom, where 232 student-athletes earned academic honors, and to the community, where USU ranked second nationally in Division I service hours, with nine teams placing in the top 10 for community service.
 Utah State is dedicated to fostering a community where all individuals feel respected, valued, and supported and where diversity of thought and culture are cultivated. We seek to recruit, hire, and retain people from all walks of life who will champion excellence in education, research, discovery, outreach, and service. We believe that promoting a strong sense of community and belonging empowers and engages all members of USU to thrive and be successful. Forbes recognized our commitment to employees when it named Utah State the best employer in Utah in 2023. Learn more about USU.
 The university provides a Dual Career Assistance Program to support careers for partners who are also seeking employment. Additionally, USU is committed to providing access and a reasonable accommodation for individuals with disabilities. To request a reasonable accommodation for a disability, contact the university’s ADA coordinator in the Office of Human Resources at 435-797-0122 or [email removed].

Description
Paid NSF Research Experiences for Undergraduates (REU) at the Smithsonian Conservation Biology Institute (Summer 2027)

Paid opportunity for enrolled undergraduates interested in expanding their conservation research experience! 
 The Smithsonian-Mason School of Conservation (SMSC) is seeking to fill 10 paid REU positions for Summer 2027 at our NSF-funded REU site titled “Saving Endangered Species and Habitats: Next-generation Education, Research, and Training for Conservation Biologists.” This 10-week REU, held from May 24 to July 30, 2027, will give undergraduate students an opportunity to conduct hands-on, full-time conservation research and gain career-ready skills to improve knowledge of and best management practices for threatened species with the goal of helping to alleviate the global extinction crisis. Students will work with mentors to develop an original inquiry-based research project within these topical areas: 1) assessing and monitoring species in the wild, 2) understanding species integrity and resilience to anthropogenic threats, and 3) improving captive management of threatened species. 

This is a fully funded, 10-week paid research experience. Candidates must be available and in residence for the entire 10-week period. All REU participants will receive a $7,000 stipend, up to $500 in travel support to/from the REU site, plus room and board at the residence and dining facilities of the Smithsonian-Mason School of Conservation (SMSC), located at the Smithsonian’s National Zoo and Conservation Biology Institute (NZCBI) in Front Royal, Virginia. 
 Who should apply? 
Undergraduate students who are very excited about a career in conservation, or interested in related disciplines, such as biology, ecology, genetics, physiology, animal behavior, endocrinology, anthropology, and environmental sciences, are encouraged to apply. 
 NSF-REU eligibility: 
To be eligible for this REU program, you must be (1) at least 18 years old, (2) enrolled in an undergraduate degree program (part-time or full-time) leading to a bachelor's or associate degree, (3) a US citizen, US national, or permanent resident.

REU funding is only available for currently enrolled undergraduate students. Undergraduate students who have graduated or will graduate by the time the REU begins (and are no longer enrolled in the university/college) are not eligible to apply. 
 When is the deadline to apply?
The deadline to apply is January 15, 2027. 

Start preparing your application materials early! Incomplete applications will not be accepted. This is a competitive program and only 10 students will be selected. Through the online application system (NSF-ETAP), students will need to submit a resume, unofficial transcripts for all college coursework, one letter of recommendation, and a one-page (single-spaced) personal essay. The essay will need to clearly describe your academic and professional interests related to the discipline of conservation and what motivated you to pursue them, as well as describe your future goals and ambitions and how this REU experience would help you achieve those goals.

Apply by following this link to the NSF application portal: https://etap.nsf.gov/

Create an account and enter SMSC in the search bar, or go directly to our program application page: https://etap.nsf.gov/award/7921/opportunity/12230

If you have specific questions, please contact the REU Faculty Program Director, Dr. Anneke DeLuycker at [email removed]

Contact
Dr. Anneke DeLuycker

Description
General Description
The Natural Resource Monitor will be a full-time, hourly employee providing construction monitoring and natural resource survey support for projects in Texas near the US/Mexico border, proximate to Presidio, Texas. The Natural Resource Monitor must be knowledgeable of the southwest border region and qualified to identify sensitive natural resources, perform nest surveys during bird nesting season, evaluate project environmental compliance with best management practices, and mark any areas for avoidance or buffer zones. 
Compensation: $30-$35/hour (plus overtime pay, full company benefits, and use of a company vehicle)
Start Date: Anticipated – ASAP (November 2026)
Duration: Anticipated – January 2028

Specific Responsibilities
The Natural Resource Monitor will conduct natural resource surveys, present environmental awareness training, and ensure compliance with environmental regulations including the Endangered Species Act, Migratory Bird Treaty Act, and project-specific environmental obligations. Minor relocation activities of plant resources may be necessary.

The Natural Resource Monitor will provide daily natural resource monitoring reports on a daily basis, inclusive of daily weather conditions, construction activities, monitoring activities, information about sensitive resource information and environmental compliance infractions, location (GPS coordinates, GIS file and Maps), and photographs.

Monitoring will occur at specific days/times to be determined through close coordination with the project team and will be based on construcction schedule.

Minimum Qualifications
• B.A. or B.S degree in biological resources, ecology, or an environmental field. Master’s Degree preferred.
• Minimum of two years of project experience providing construction monitoring support in the southwest border region within the field of environmental compliance, biological, and/or natural resources.
• Positive references from industry or government for previous monitoring duties must be provided.
• Familiar with the project area or similar environs and knowledge of habitat and wildlife species (common, special status, endangered, threatened, etc.) near the project area.
• Familiar with ArcGIS Field Maps and Survey123.
• Ability to pass a background check and obtain government security clearance.
• Valid US Driver's License.
• Valid State Social Security Number or Alien Registration Number.

How To Apply
Please send resume and cover letter detailing relevant experience and references to Arnaud Kerisit at [email removed].

Description
 Agency:  University of Georgia 
Location: Athens, GA 
Job Category: Data Analyst 
Salary: $60,000/year plus full UGA benefits package (NOTE: This is a 6-month position) 
Start Date: January 1st, 2027 (6-month position with possibility of Ph.D. [contingent on funding]) 
Last Date to Apply: Application review begins November 16, open until candidate selected 
Website: Home - UGA Deer Lab | Kohl Lab 
Contacts: Marcelo Jorge ([email removed]), Michel Kohl ([email removed]) 
 Description: This position is part of an interdisciplinary project at the University of Georgia (UGA) led by Drs. Kohl and Jorge in the Warnell School of Forestry and Natural Resources, funded through the Wheatley Interdisciplinary Faculty Seed Grant Program. The project is a collaborative effort involving state wildlife agencies, university partners, and the Rocky Mountain Elk Foundation (RMEF) aimed and understanding how elk habitat management treatments impact nutrition and population vital rates for eastern elk. Through this position you will develop collaborations with agency and RMEF personnel while collecting, cleaning, and analyzing historical treatment data to inform efficient study design and field work logistics planning. This position is not permitted for remote work. Travel will be required to visit field sites. NOTE: This position is only funded for 6 months. 
 Qualifications: Applicants should have an expressed interest in Eastern elk populations, habitat management, genetics, and/or nutrition. Applicants must have completed a Master’s degree in wildlife management or related field and shown a propensity for R coding, GIS, as well as a strong publication record. Applicants must be able to pass a UGA background check and driving records check.

Description
Position Summary:

One Ecologist/Forestry Researcher (Full-time, 40 hrs/week) position available with Colorado State University (CSU) Center for Environmental Management of Military Lands (CEMML). This position is part of CEMML’s Early-Career Development Program, which helps emerging professionals bridge academic learning and career success through hands-on experience, mentorship, and professional development. To learn more visit: Early-Career Development Program - CEMML.


This is a research focus position. The role will use GIS and remotely sensed data, along with Forest Inventory and Analysis (FIA) data to characterize, map, model and analyze tree species composition and related forest attributes in a tropical environment. This will aid in understanding forest ecosystem disturbance and resilience.


For full consideration, please apply by Monday, November 16, 2026, 11:59 PM (MT). 


Essential Job Duties:

Combine existing spatial data with additional predictor variables developed as needed, with Forest Inventory and Analysis (FIA) data to characterize and map spatial gradients in tree species composition and related forest attributes.

Evaluate whether mapped outputs or model derived spatial predictors can reduce uncertainties in FIA estimates of tree species basal area, biomass, or related composition metrics through one or more model assisted estimation approaches.

Link mapped species composition outputs to an existing dataset of fire occurrences to characterize tree species composition where fires occurred, including areas where field surveys of tree species are not available.

Develop a comparison of uncertainties in FIA estimates of species basal area, biomass, or related composition metrics when estimates are based only on FIA plots versus when model assisted estimation uses mapped auxiliary information.

Create maps of model derived species composition gradients, or related composition outputs.

Model derived composition values for places where fires occurred, along with related charts that help characterize the species composition of forests where fires occur.


Decision Making:

Determine and develop appropriate model parameters.

Determine appropriate spatial predictor data sets.


Supervision:

Does not supervise.


Conditions of Employment:

Successful completion of CSU’s standard pre-employment background check.

Minimum Qualifications:

PhD in Systems Ecology or related field, including coursework in ecology, ecosystem climatology, statistics, spatial statistics, machine learning, applied bioinformatics, data visualization, geographic information systems and science communication.

One year experience in systems ecology, including work in GIS and remote sensing and FIA plot data in tropical islands of the US.

Experience as first author publishing a refereed journal article in a top journal focused on research typically requiring geospatial data and analysis (e.g., Remote Sensing or Ecological Indicators).

Experience with programming languages including R and Python.


Preferred Qualifications:

Experience developing spatial or statistical models of forest composition, biomass, basal area, or related ecological attributes.

Experience applying model-assisted estimation or other methods that integrate forest inventory data with auxiliary spatial information.

Experience integrating remote sensing, climate, topographic, fire, or other disturbance data in geospatial analyses.

Advanced proficiency using R, Python, and GIS for spatial modeling, uncertainty analysis, visualization, and reproducible workflows.

Experience communicating geospatial research through peer-reviewed publications, technical reports, maps, or presentations.

Contact
CEMML ECDP

Description

Fisheries Ecology Positions

Two contractor opportunities  |  B.S. and M.S. levels

Quantitative and Conservation Ecology Team  •  U.S. Geological Survey  •  Columbia, Missouri

Position Description
The Quantitative and Conservation Ecology (QCE) team at the U.S. Geological Survey Columbia Environmental Research Center is seeking two student-services contractors to support a broad portfolio of freshwater fisheries research. We anticipate hiring one early-career biologist who is nearing completion of, or has recently completed, a B.S. degree and a second biologist who is nearing completion of, or has recently completed, an M.S. degree.

Both individuals will contribute to multiple projects rather than a single assigned study. Research occurs in the Great Lakes, Mississippi River basin, and other river systems, with the balance of field, laboratory, and analytical activities varying by season and project needs.

Research Areas
·  Fish movement and habitat use: acoustic, radio, and PIT telemetry studies examining movement, survival, habitat selection, and connectivity.
·  River restoration and barrier effects: evaluating fish movements and community responses to dam removal, passage improvements, and other restoration actions, including work in the Cuyahoga River watershed.
·  Invasive species and fisheries sampling: invasive carp monitoring and removal, gear comparisons, sampling efficiency, and standardized fish surveys in large rivers and tributaries.
·  Population and community ecology: assessment of fish distributions, occupancy, abundance, survival, and recruitment using field observations and quantitative approaches.
·  Methods development and experimental research: side-scan sonar, habitat mapping, controlled field or pond experiments, and complementary monitoring techniques.

Types of Services Required

Field Activities

·  Deploy, maintain, and retrieve acoustic receivers, PIT equipment, radio telemetry systems, and other monitoring gear.
·  Conduct active fish tracking and standardized field sampling from boats, kayaks, and shorelines using appropriate sampling gear.
·  Collect biological and environmental measurements, maintain field records, and assist with fish handling and sample processing.
·  Participate in gear evaluation trials, habitat surveys, and aquatic research experiments.
·  Operate or learn to operate small vessels, trailers, and field equipment safely; participate in overnight and multi-day field assignments as required by the position.


Data, Laboratory, and Research Activities

·  Download, organize, verify, and manage fisheries, telemetry, and environmental datasets.
·  Process spatial and sonar data and develop maps, tables, figures, and descriptive summaries.
·  Assist with analyses in R or other appropriate software, according to training and project needs.
·  Support reports, data releases, and project documentation; contribute to scientific manuscripts when appropriate to the assigned scope of work.

Expectations by Position Level
B.S.-level position: This is a field-intensive position requiring substantial travel. The selected contractor should expect frequent trips to study sites away from Columbia, including overnight travel and multi-day field assignments, especially during peak field seasons. Responsibilities emphasize high-quality field data collection, equipment maintenance, data management, and collaborative research. Candidates who recently graduated or are finishing a B.S. degree are encouraged to apply.

M.S.-level position: Travel to field sites, including overnight trips, is required, but generally less frequent than for the B.S.-level position. The position may be structured as administrative support or research, depending on the successful candidate’s qualifications and the responsibilities of the award.

·  Administrative-support classification: Emphasis on coordinating project activities, supporting fieldwork, managing and quality-checking data, and preparing technical materials. Independent manuscript development or publication is not expected.
·  Research classification: For candidates with demonstrated analytical and scientific writing skills and an interest in research. Work includes substantive data analysis, interpretation, scientific writing, and development of manuscripts and other research products. Publication depends on project needs and timelines.

Both positions contribute to ongoing team projects. Actual assignments will reflect each individual’s experience and demonstrated skills, the contracted scope of work, and team priorities.

Project Ownership and Professional Development
Both positions offer opportunities to take ownership of components of ongoing projects and develop professionally. Contractors whose assignments include research responsibilities may also contribute to publications and complementary research questions aligned with team objectives. Opportunities to present findings at professional conferences may be available if desired, if funding is available, and if the work aligns with project and team priorities. Conference participation and publication are not guaranteed; publication is not an expectation of the M.S. administrative-support classification.

Qualifications
Applicants should have completed, or be nearing completion of, a degree in fisheries, ecology, biology, environmental science, natural resources, or a closely related discipline. The two positions are intended for different educational stages, as described above.


Required

·  Experience with, or relevant preparation for, aquatic field research and careful biological data collection.
·  Ability and willingness to work safely in and around water and to learn appropriate boating and field procedures.
·  Basic computer proficiency, including spreadsheets, data entry, and file management.
·  Good organizational, communication, and interpersonal skills for working in a collaborative team.
·  Valid driver’s license and ability to undertake overnight work travel.


Preferred, but not required

·  Experience with acoustic, radio, or PIT telemetry; electrofishing or other fisheries sampling gear; or side-scan sonar.
·  Experience operating, trailering, or backing boats.
·  Experience with R, GIS, statistical analyses, database management, or scientific writing.

Working Conditions
Work is based in Columbia, Missouri, with field assignments at study sites in multiple states. The B.S.-level position requires frequent travel and substantial time away from the duty station during field seasons. The M.S.-level position requires travel as well, including overnight assignments, but generally less frequently. Fieldwork may involve early mornings, long workdays, and occasional extended work periods. Conditions can include heat, cold, rain, strong currents, debris, muddy terrain, insects, and uneven or unstable shorelines. Duties may require lifting and carrying equipment weighing up to approximately 50 pounds. Lodging and travel-related expenses for authorized official travel will be addressed in accordance with applicable contract and government travel requirements.

Compensation and Appointment
These are student-services contractor opportunities, not federal government employment positions. The calendar year 2026 direct-purchase-order hourly rates for the Columbia, Missouri duty station are:

·  B.S. degree: $21.01 per hour.
·  B.S. with superior academic achievement, or B.S. plus one year of graduate study: $26.03 per hour.
·  M.S. administrative-support classification: $31.83 per hour.
·  M.S. research classification: $38.52 per hour.

The final hourly rate will reflect the contracted level of responsibility and expectations, verified qualifying education and credentials, the rate schedule applicable at the time of award, and contracting approval. In particular, the M.S. research rate is associated with substantive research and scientific-product expectations; the M.S. administrative-support rate does not carry an expectation of independently developing publishable science. Applicants nearing graduation are encouraged to apply, but degree-based rates depend on completion of the qualifying education. Contractors are responsible for applicable taxes and for transportation and living expenses at the principal duty station. The anticipated appointment is approximately one year, with possible extension dependent on funding and research needs. Start dates are flexible.

Principal Duty Station
U.S. Geological Survey, Columbia Environmental Research Center
 4200 New Haven Road, Columbia, MO 65201

How to Apply
Applications will be reviewed as they are received. Initial interviews are expected in early December 2026. Both positions will remain open until filled. Applicants are encouraged to apply even after the initial interview period, as one or both positions may still be available.

Email a cover letter, resume or CV, and an unofficial transcript to Matthew R. Acre at [email removed]. In the cover letter, indicate whether you wish to be considered for the B.S.-level or M.S.-level position, your anticipated or completed graduation date, and your earliest available start date. Briefly describe relevant field, analytical, or research experience and interests. M.S.-level applicants interested in a research-focused assignment should highlight their quantitative, scientific writing, and research experience.

Selected applicants may be asked to provide an official transcript and complete required contractor registration, including obtaining a Unique Entity ID (UEI), before beginning work. A UEI is available without charge. Questions may be directed to [email removed] or 573-890-0300.

Contact
Matthew Acre
[email removed] (preferred contact method)

Description
The Maria Mitchell Association (MMA) is offering two intern positions at its Natural Science Museum for the 2027 summer. The Natural Science Museum is divided into an Aquatics Room housing numerous freshwater and brackish water animals, a Herpetology Room housing snakes, frogs, and turtles, a Collections Room that displays various animal specimens from across Nantucket, and lastly a STEM Activity Room where guests can learn about science through hands-on activities. 


A unique position and a unique museum allows the intern to learn everything that goes into running a natural science museum. This paid internship immerses the intern into all facets of museum operations, which includes animal husbandry, animal collection, exhibit and signage design, educational programming, volunteer management, collections preservation, leading tours, gift shop management, and much more. 


The ideal candidate should have an interest in biology, ecology, and/or environmental education. Many former MMA Natural Science Museum interns are working in the fields of outdoor education, animal husbandry, environmental education, veterinary medicine, K-12 science education, STEM graduate school, environmental technicians, and environmental stewardship.



The 2027 Natural Science Museum Internship application period will open February 1, 2027 at 11PM EST.


Completed applications consist of a resume, cover letter, 3 references and 2 letters of recommendation, official or unofficial transcripts and the digital Internship application.

Description
The Institute for Applied Ecology is a mission-driven non-profit organization that works to restore species and save ecosystems. Founded in 1999, IAE fills a unique niche in conservation and works with a diverse group of partners to conserve native species and habitats through restoration, research and education. Our team of botanists, ecologists, educators, and restoration professionals advances our mission across the western U.S. from our headquarters in Corvallis, Oregon and our branch office in Santa Fe, New Mexico.

Position Description
The Restoration Ecologist contributes to IAE’s conservation mission by leading and implementing several habitat enhancement and restoration projects that support the conservation and recovery of rare plants, wildlife, and broader ecosystems. Projects are located in several ecoregions throughout the Pacific Northwest, with a primary focus in the Willamette Valley and Coast Range of Oregon. The ecologist will develop strong relationships with project partners, contribute to and lead development of restoration plans, and implement restoration activities using a variety of techniques to achieve project deliverables and IAE’s conservation goals.
 The Restoration Ecologist is part of a collaborative and passionate Northwest Habitat Restoration team, which works alongside ecologists in IAE’s Conservation Research and Plant Materials programs.

Specific Responsibilities
Project Management and Implementation: Lead habitat restoration activities at public and private land conservation sites for assigned projects.  
Manage all aspects of restoration planning and implementation. Lead or assist with preparation of restoration, planting, and management plans. Provide contract and budget oversight and communication, and secure permits as needed.
Ensure successful completion of restoration treatments including mowing, brush clearing, solarization, herbicide application, burning, planting, and seeding.  
Operate, supervise, and ensure safe use of equipment (e.g., weed-eaters, chainsaws, tractors, mowers, discs, and seeders).  Maintain restoration equipment, power tools and storage areas.
Use ArcGIS platforms to map project activities, invasive species, and navigate to remote sites.
Monitor restoration sites and impacts of treatments through site assessments and vegetation inventories. Process, analyze and report data, and maintain restoration databases. 
Coordination and Supervision: 
Help oversee/coordinate habitat restoration field technicians’ work.  
Prepare contracts, hire, schedule, and supervise contractors, seasonal work crews, and volunteers. 
Coordinate work with other IAE staff, including extensive seeding efforts, nursery production, acquisition, and outplanting of large quantities of plant materials.
Communications, Writing, and Outreach:  
Prepare reports for funding agencies, newsletter articles and other IAE publications.
Build and maintain connections with partners, funders, and private landowners.
Conduct tours, workshops, and presentations for funders, partners, and the public.  
Assist in the preparation of grant proposals and help to acquire funding to support restoration projects, including the drafting of project budgets and narratives. 
 Minimum Qualifications
·         Bachelor’s degree in botany, biology, wildlife, horticulture, ecology, or related work with five years of post-degree experience.
·         Positive attitude with excellent oral and written communication skills, including experience developing and maintaining relationships with partners, private landowners, and colleagues.
·         Strong organizational skills and attention to detail. 
·         Experience preparing planning documents, including restoration, planting, maintenance, and management plans.
·         Plant identification skills (including common weeds).
·         Demonstrated proficiency with Microsoft Office (Word, Excel, PowerPoint), Google Suite, and ArcGIS.
·         Navigational and mapping skills using tools such as aerial photos, compass, GPS, and mapping applications (e.g., ArcGIS Pro and AGOL).
·         Ability to obtain (within three months of hire) an Oregon commercial pesticide applicator’s license (agriculture category).
·         Good physical condition and ability to work long hours in adverse weather conditions, including potential exposure to poison oak.
·         Ability to hike up to 3 miles carrying a 40-pound pack and work in a bent-over/kneeling/sitting position for long periods of time
·         Ability to remain in a stationary position, often sitting or standing for prolonged periods
·         Willingness to operate an ATV and other restoration equipment as needed.
·         Current U.S. driver’s license and clean driving record.
 Preferred Qualifications
·         Master’s degree and/or additional education in one of the same areas
Familiarity with Willamette Valley plant communities and habitat requirements for prairie wildlife, including pollinators and grassland birds.
·         Experience with contract development and oversight, project planning and implementation, budgeting, and permitting.
Holds an Oregon Pesticide Applicators license.
·         Experience collecting native seed. 
·         Familiarity with nonprofit organizations and a demonstrated record of successful grant proposals.

 Our organization:
The FWC envisions a Florida where fish and wildlife are abundant and thriving in healthy and connected natural landscapes with vital working lands and waterways; where natural resources are valued and safely enjoyed by all; and wherein natural systems support vibrant human communities and a strong economy.
Our Mission: Managing fish and wildlife resources for their long-term well-being and the benefit of people.
Every organization has an identity that is forged not only by what it does, but by how it conducts itself.  The values embedded in our mission and expressed in the vision of the FWC are to make quality decisions by being dynamic, science-informed, efficient, ethical, collaborative and committed to the vitality of the state and its environment.

7 years professional experience in a closely-related biological field or laboratory program can substitute for the required bachelor’s degree.

 Preferred Qualifications: Preference will be given to candidates with the following qualifications:

A bachelor's degree from an accredited college or university with major course of study in one of the biological sciences and three years of professional biological experience in a closely-related field or laboratory program; or
 A master's degree from an accredited college or university with major course of study in one of the biological sciences and two years professional biological experience in a closely-related field or laboratory program; or
 A doctorate from an accredited college or university with major course of study in one of the biological sciences and one year of professional biological experience in a closely-related field or laboratory program can substitute for the required experience. 
 Requirements:
Employment in this position is contingent upon a satisfactory criminal history check. The criminal history check must be completed prior to or within the first thirty days of employment.

Position Overview and Responsibilities:
Lake Okeechobee is a world-renowned freshwater fishery that supports multiple communities and is the headwaters of the Florida Everglades.  This position serves as the lead biologist for the Division of Freshwater Fisheries Management (DFFM) for Lake Okeechobee.

The selected candidate will represent the Division on issues concerning Lake Okeechobee and surrounding watersheds and provide input to South Florida Water Management District and U.S. Army Corps of Engineers on Lake Okeechobee water level management and schedules.  

Establish and maintain stakeholder contacts with anglers, fish camps, local governmental officials, fishing guides, outdoor media, and fishing clubs to ensure effective, two-way communication relative to FWC programs and projects.  

Coordinate with Regional Freshwater Fisheries Administrator and Division of Habitat and Species Conservation (HSC) staff to develop aquatic restoration, enhancement, aquatic plant management, and other projects that emphasize improving or maintaining sport fish populations, angler access or the creation of new fishing opportunities.  

Assist Regional Freshwater Fisheries staff in developing partnerships in aquatic resource management projects with federal, state and local agencies and stakeholders; serve as DFFM representative on intra- and inter-agency groups as assigned; administer the Lake Okeechobee commercial haul seine program for the Division; and collaborate with HSC’s Aquatic Habitat Restoration and Enhancement and Invasive Plant Management personnel to maintain expertise in those areas.  

Conduct surveys and assist with fish community and angler utilization sampling; identify ongoing and proposed aquatic restoration, enhancement or aquatic plant management sites to determine actual or potential effects to freshwater sportfish population; handle data compilation and analysis to inform management decisions; compose necessary reports to meet the needs of state and federal level reporting. 
 This position is responsible for supervising two seasonal part-time creel clerks.

Description
The Opportunity
As the Aquatic Invasive Species Coordinator, you will provide both regional and project-specific coordination, implementation, and quality assurance of invasive species management projects. Facilitate the use of standardized methodologies for data collection and analysis of pre and post project conditions. This position offers an opportunity to lead field operations, coordinate research and demonstration projects, and contribute to protecting New York State's aquatic ecosystems.


Key Responsibilities:
Developing and acquiring permits for actions pursuant to Aquatic Invasive Species (AIS)  management directly undertaken within the region.
Executing regional early detection-rapid response program, including site prioritization and coordination of monitoring in lacustrine and riverine systems.
Utilizing a variety of methods and technologies (eDNA, UAS, etc.) to enhance early detection capacity.
Coordinating the Cayuga Lake Hydrilla Control Project, including planning, application, and management of herbicides.
Working closely with regional lake associations to promote the development and implementation of lake management plans and watercraft inspection steward programs.
Participating in regional, state-wide, and federal collaboratives to promote exchange of information throughout the watershed.

This is a full-time (40 hours/week), one-year term Contract College position based in Cortland, NY, with the possibility of extension. This position is fully on-site. Standard business hours; however, work schedules may vary during peak field seasons.


About the Department of Biological and Environmental Engineering
The Department of Biological and Environmental Engineering (BEE) is one of the largest of its kind in the country with a very diverse faculty, staff, and student population. The department serves three integrated functions: teaching undergraduate and graduate students, researching problems in biology and the environment, and public outreach to help society implement new knowledge.

The New York State Water Resources Institute (NYSWRI) resides within the College of Agriculture and Life Sciences (CALS) and BEE. Its mission is to improve the management of water resources in New York State and the nation. NYSWRI collaborates with regional, state, and national partners to increase awareness of emerging water resource issues and to develop and assess new water resource management approaches, technologies, and policies. NYSWRI connects water research and water management communities.


What We Need
We are seeking a talented professional who excels at building and maintaining strong, collaborative relationships with diverse stakeholders and brings knowledge of aquatic invasive species and their management. Additionally, you will have: 

A Bachelor’s Degree and 3+ years of relevant experience in aquatic biology, ecology, natural resources, environmental studies or equivalent combination of education and experience.
Experience in one or more of the following involving aquatic invasive species: field work in waterbodies and wetlands involving surveys, general data collection and analysis, and management.
Experience incorporating the perspectives of multiple communities. 
Proven ability to work in a multicultural environment is critical.
Excellent written and oral communication skills.
Excellent organizational experience.
Ability to provide consistent and accurate information.
Experience managing multiple projects, schedules, and priorities in a deadline-driven environment.
Flexibility and receptiveness to new ideas and approaches.
A proactive approach to independently identifying and following up on program objectives, organizational needs, determining tasks necessary to meet project requirements and deadlines, and engaging and collaborating with support staff and resources as needed with minimal supervision.
New York State pesticide application certification in category 5a; or, pesticide application certification in any category with a willingness to obtain category 5a certification within one year of hire; or, 2+ years of verifiable experience as a technician in any commercial category with a willingness to upgrade to category 5a certification within one year of hire; or, willingness to become a technician in category 5A once hired and upgrade to a commercial applicator within 1 year of hire (candidates with no prior pesticide application experience).
Demonstrated geospatial analysis and visualization skills (e.g., ArcGIS, ArcPRO, ArcGIS Online).
Experience and proficiency with operation and maintenance of motorboats and other mechanical equipment.
Experience with report preparation and analysis.
Experience demonstrating sound judgment, creativity, research, and problem-solving skills.
Willingness and demonstrated aptitude for supervising others.
Ability to meet the travel requirements of the position, including access to reliable transportation and maintenance of a valid, unrestricted New York State driver’s license.
Proven experience connecting inclusion, belonging and wellbeing practices to business goals. 


If you possess these experiences and skills this may be the role for you! There are a few other qualifications we would view as incredibly helpful in this role, to include: 
Master’s degree in aquatic biology, ecology, natural resources, environmental studies or equivalent, with at least 2 years of relevant professional experience.
Familiarity with state and federal permitting processes, including Article 15, Article 24, and State Environmental Quality Review (SEQR).


A cover letter and resume are required for consideration for this position.
